report.markdown:
# Birthplace and Proposal Year of the Inventor of the World Wide Web

## Overview

One source reports that the inventor of the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee, was born in London and first proposed the system in 1989. [1] Specifically, one source reports that he submitted his proposal for the World Wide Web to CERN in March 1989. [2]

## Sources

1. [Tim Berners-Lee - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Berners-Lee) — wikipedia.org, published 2001-05-15, fetched 2026-10-31
2. [World Wide Web - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Web) — wikipedia.org, published 2001-11-01, fetched 2026-10-31

Specifically, one source reports that he submitted his proposal for the World Wide Web to CERN in March 1989.

stats.title: Birthplace and Proposal Year of the Inventor of the World Wide Web

claims.text: Tim Berners-Lee was born in London on 8 June 1955.
claims.reason: Supported by only 1 independent origin(s); 2 required.

evidence.quote: Berners-Lee was born in London on 8 June 1955, the son of the mathematicians and computer scientists Mary Lee Berners-Lee ( née Woods; 1924–2017) and Conway Berners-Lee (1921–2019).

claims.text: Tim Berners-Lee proposed an information management system, which became the World Wide Web, on 12 March 1989.
claims.reason: Supported by only 1 independent origin(s); 2 required.

evidence.quote: Berners-Lee proposed an information management system on 12 March 1989 and implemented the first successful communication between a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) client and server via the Internet in mid-November.

claims.text: Tim Berners-Lee submitted a proposal for the World Wide Web to CERN in March 1989.
claims.reason: Supported by only 1 independent origin(s); 2 required.

evidence.quote: Berners-Lee submitted a proposal to CERN in March 1989, without giving the system a name.
